chapter: Opening and the Buddy Petit band
title: Buddy Petit's drinking and the unpaid Bogalusa job
summary: Buddy Petit was easy-going but drank heavily; Zardis tells how Petit confronted a man who had not paid the band and got the money next day.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And can you tell us any more about Buddy Patti since he's not here anymore? I never did get to hear him.

What did he sound like? I know it's hard to explain. Buddy was a nice fella. He was an easy going fella. But he had nice ways, you know what I mean, until he'd get that booze. And he used to like to drink plenty. You know what I mean? He was a man that would drink and would take two tree jobs at one time. Well George Lewis told me that once. Well that's the facts you see. And that's what the ruination of the band. But the people used to like him. Buddy did some things there. I think if somebody else would do that now I think somebody would kill him. You know what I mean? But they just liked him. He was just lucky. And I see one night we played up in Burgalusi and after we played up there the mayor or the sheriff, somebody, didn't pay us the money that night because he told us that they didn't make no money. He said, but you come around tomorrow I'm going to pay you all the more or I'm going to drive down to Covington and pay you money. Buddy got, but he said all right at the first time you know. He pulled around there and started drinking that old corn liquor made last night. That was in probation then. Yeah that was. And Buddy got full of that liquor there. He said come on, drive me to the man. He studied a lot.
Did he stutter all the time? All the time studied. Yes he studied.

Maybe somebody told me. Yes he did. He studied all the time. He said I want you to bring me to the man's house. I want some money. All right. He gets on there and said come on we're going to the man's house. I said we got him in the car and went on down to the man's house. I mean he went to the man's and knocked at the door. Man said who was that? Buddy Petit. So man said what you want buddy? I want some money. So that's where the man said I told you I didn't have no money buddy. Yeah. So he came down and he started talking. He was a nice fellow through the man. So he told the sheriff. He said, oh buddy I told you I don't have no money here. He said now wait until the moron I'll give you some money. He said I'll have some money right now. So the sheriff said wait let me see if my wife got any money. That man had to go back there. He just had $20. He said that's all my wife got $20. He said I'm going to give you this $20. And tomorrow he said don't come here. I'm going to come down to the covenant and bring the rest of that money you know. So sure enough man in the morning the man around 10 11 o'clock he came down there and he told Buddy. He said, Buddy I didn't talk to you to come to my house and wake me up for a few niggas like that. Buddy said I need my money. They said yeah Buddy. He said all them boys need their money too just like you needed but you should have you know should have waited until like I told you and then you would have got the money. So he asked us did we get our money Buddy paid? I said yeah he paid us. Well that's one thing about Buddy. He you know he pay you money. You know what I mean? If he gets you on the job like he said well the job paid so much so much you know. And enough he don't have it if he doesn't spend the money he's going to say well I didn't spend the money and I'm going to have to owe you. Is it all right? Well quite nicely he spent it. You didn't pledge you didn't know that. But it's got to be all right. You know what I mean? So but finally he's a pretty good fella. Buddy was all right.
